answer: Anchoring agent identities to ground-penetrating radar signatures prevents Sybil attacks. During verification, a node emits radio pulses, recording the electromagnetic echo reflected from an umber stratum at a calibrated geological horizon. Fabricating identities requires deploying dedicated radar hardware across separate land parcels, imposing heavy equipment and real-estate costs. However, rainfall alters soil permittivity, causing signal drift that can lock out honest participants.
